ios.desc:
Kabit: Streak-Based Habit Tracking With 50,000+ Users (4.7/5 Avg ratings)

Build habits without making habit tracking feel like another chore.

Kabit helps you start small, stay consistent, and see your progress over time. Create simple daily habits, track streaks, set reminders, and use widgets to keep your goals visible throughout the day.

Whether you want to build a new routine, stay focused, journal your progress, or gently get back on track after missing a day, Kabit keeps the experience clean and practical.

Features:

- Track daily habits and streaks
- Set custom reminders
- View progress by week, month, and year
- Add journal notes and photos
- Use widgets for quick habit tracking
- Review stats and progress insights
- Rearrange, archive, import, and export habits
- Choose themes and supported languages

Kabit is designed for small wins. No clutter, no pressure, just a simple place to build routines that fit your real life.

Privacy Policy: https://kabitapp.com/privacy

quotes.text: I have used a lot of habit-tracking apps and most of them are filled with features that are not useful to me, sometimes UI is a mess etc. I wanted to build an app that was simple and useful. I wasn't sure about GPT ability but wanted to give it a try. There was a lot of trial and error, especially in figuring out the logic of the streak counter, which took a lot of time. I have spent some time polishing the UI as well. Although not a perfect app, I think I have a good tracker. I am planning to add more features and would love to know your thoughts and feedback. Thanks

quotes.text:
Hi HN, I'm Rahul, and I come from a design background. I've always wanted to create my own app, but my lack of coding skills held me back. Fortunately, with AI advancement, I was finally able to get started.

I wanted to track my habits, but most trackers on the App Store offered features I didn't need. I simply wanted to track whether I completed or missed my habits, see basic stats about missed days, and have a streak indicator for motivation. This is what sparked my journey.

Initially, even setting up the project in Xcode was confusing. It took countless back-and-forth sessions to establish proper file architecture. Since tools like Cursor and Windsurf weren't mainstream yet, I constantly relied on ChatGPT (and later Claude) to generate and fix code.

A couple of months after launch, a popular Middle Eastern influencer randomly promoted my app on Instagram to her followers. My app suddenly had over 500 reviews in just one week. Unfortunately, I knew nothing about paywall testing or pricing strategy, so I couldn't fully capitalize on this momentum.

This experience launched me into learning about marketing, testing different approaches, and adding features customers requested. I'm incredibly proud of what I built and have since created five more apps.

What Makes Kabit Different
